chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, who said, 'I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him)'; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who both said, 'We asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him)'

about a man who bequeathed a 'portion' (sahm) from his wealth, and we do not know what this 'portion' is. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there not with you, among what has reached you from Ja'far (peace be upon him) nor from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), anything regarding it?' We said to him (peace be upon him), 'May we be sacrificed for you! We have not heard our companions mentioning anything of this from your forefathers (peace be upon him).'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The 'portion' is one from eight.' So we said to him (peace be upon him), 'May we be sacrificed for you! How did it become one from eight?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not read the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I do read it, but I do not know which place it is.'

The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The charities are only for the poor and the needy, and the officials appointed over them, and those whose hearts are made to incline (to Truth) and the (ransoming of) captives and those in debts and in the Way of Allah and the wayfarer.'

Then he (peace be upon him) made (the number) eight with his hand, and said: 'And similarly, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) divided it upon eight portions. Therefore, the 'portion' is one from eight.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a 'portion' (sahm) in Islamic bequests according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) resolves the ambiguity of a bequest specifying only a 'portion' by defining it as one of the eight categories of zakat recipients mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah. He establishes this by citing the Quranic verse and demonstrating how the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) historically divided wealth into these eight equal shares, thereby providing a clear jurisprudential precedent for inheritance and charity distribution in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan who said, ‘I asked Al Reza asws’; and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Safwan and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who both said,

‘We asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about a man who bequeathed with a ‘portion’ from his wealth, and we do not know the ‘portion’, which this is it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there not with you among what has reached you neither from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> nor Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> anything with regards to it?’ We said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May we be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! We have not hear our companions mentioning anything from this, from you<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup>’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The ‘portion’ is one from eight (1/8)’. So we said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May we be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How did it come to be one from eight?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Have you nor read the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I have read it, but I do not know in which place it is’.

So heasws said: ‘The Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [9:60] But rather, the charities are only for the poor and the needy, and the officials (appointed) over them, and those whose hearts are made to incline (to Truth) and the (ransoming of) captives and those in debts and in the Way of Allah and the wayfarer’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> made (the number) eight by his hand, and said: ‘And similarly, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> divided it upon eight portions. Therefore, the ‘portion’ is one from eight’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Safwan from abu af-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who have said the following: “We once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who has made a will about a share of his legacy and it is not known how much a share is. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Have you not received anything about it from Ja‘far, or abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhim al-Salam?’ We replied, ‘We pray to Allah to keep our souls in service for your cause, we have not heard our people mention anything about it from your ancestors.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘A share is one of eight.’ We said, ‘We pray to Allah to keep our souls in service for your cause, how it has become one of eight?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Have you not read the book of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious?’ I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I read but do not know in which passage it is.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘It is in the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, “Charity is only for the poor, destitute, Zakat collectors, people inclined to the religion, slaves, debtors, in the way of Allah and for those who deplete their supplies on a journey.” [9:60]’

He (the Imam) then formed eight with his hand and said, ‘This is how the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, distributed in eight shares, thus, a share is one out of eight.’”
